title: Execution of a sequentially composed protocol
statement:
Let $p$ be a finite-message protocol with input types $X$, $Y$ and output type $\alpha$, and let $q$ assign to each value $a \in \alpha$ a finite-message protocol $q(a)$ with the same input types and output type $\beta$. For any inputs $x \in X$ and $y \in Y$, executing the sequential composition of $p$ with $q$ agrees with first running $p$ on $(x,y)$ to obtain an output $a$ and then running $q(a)$ on the same inputs:
\[
  \mathrm{run}\bigl(\mathrm{bind}(p,q)\bigr)(x,y) \;=\; \mathrm{run}\bigl(q(\mathrm{run}(p)(x,y))\bigr)(x,y).
\]
hypotheses_covered: a finite-message protocol p over inputs X, Y with output type α
a continuation q from α to protocols with output type β
replaced:
For any protocol $p$, continuation $q$, and inputs $x \in X$, $y \in Y$,
\[
  (\texttt{bind}\;p\;q).\texttt{run}\;x\;y
  \;=\; (q\,(p.\texttt{run}\;x\;y)).\texttt{run}\;x\;y.
\]
